dataset.correction: Provenance-only. source-licenses.md was byte-identical to the three-source partial snapshot's file: it stated the release contained records from three sources only and listed Salesforce/xlam-function-calling-60k under 'Sources not in this release', while the payload carries 57,342 xLAM records. It is rewritten for the four-source payload, and CITATIONS.bib gains the APIGen entry the release manifest declares as required for xLAM. Parquet bytes, the 176-shard set, the record count and the corpus fingerprint are unchanged; no data file was written.

revision_chain_since_previous_record.what: Intermediate revision: source-licenses.md corrected, CITATIONS.bib not yet. The correction was published as two Hub commits rather than one atomic commit, so this half-applied state existed and is recorded rather than tidied away.
Card corrected against committed artifacts, from the OpenGrad claim audit of 2026-09-13. Published without a publication record, which left every recorded revision stale for three days.

reconstruction_evidence.immutable_because: A Hugging Face revision is content-addressed: the identifier names the exact tree state that was published on that date. It is the same identifier the hub_revision field records, so the reconstruction names the artifact it describes rather than a summary of it.

why_this_record_exists: A metadata correction to a frozen release previously left no trace. The release payload is immutable; the published bundle is not, and a repository whose discipline is that identities never move silently needs both recorded separately.
notes: This entry did not exist contemporaneously with the event it records. It was written on 2026-09-14 about a publication that happened on 2026-09-13, and it says so in machine-readable fields rather than only in prose: event_occurred_at, entry_recorded_at and recorded_retroactively distinguish when the event happened from when it was written down.

Committed records keep the namespace they were written with, so the 2026-09-11 publication of this repository is recorded under arrochi112/. The two names resolve to the same repository, and the revision chain is validated across the rename.
No shard was written and no record count changed. That is the point of recording this separately from a release: a provenance correction is not a new version of the corpus.
